items.title: Re-vendor LibKa0s v1.71.0 from the local tag; record the unrecorded v1.69.0/v1.70.0 span; kit 38 clears the Totals/badge mismatch
items.spec: Follow /dev-copilot:wow-revendor-libka0s mechanically (OWNER_SCOPE 5: no interview, no issue filing). (1) Payload: copy ../LibKa0s at the LOCAL tag v1.71.0 (`git -C ../LibKa0s archive v1.71.0` or a detached worktree, never the LibKa0s working tree) whole into libs/LibKa0s/ (LibKa0s/ payload incl. LibKa0s.xml) and tests/_kit/ (testkit/), deleting files the tag no longer ships. Kit.VERSION in tests/_kit/framework.lua becomes 38. (2) CLAUDE.md provenance line `Bundles [LibKa0s](...) v1.70.0 (MIT).` -> v1.71.0, same commit. (3) Regenerate docs/test-cases.md with kit 38: the Totals table no longer counts the declared skip (AT-R-07: was Total 877 vs badge 876/876); Total now equals the README badge figure, and the skip sits on a `| Skipped | 1 |` row. If the badge figure differs from the new Total, roll the badge. (4) Unrecorded-tag record (AT-A-01, cluster C03): v1.69.0 (commit 5075fd5) and v1.70.0 (4c16982) were vendored with no docs/revendor/ bundle; the newest recorded bundle is docs/revendor/2026-10-04-v1.68.1/. Write ONE consolidated span bundle docs/revendor/<today>-v1.69.0-v1.70.0/ in the shape of docs/revendor/2026-10-01-v1.64.0-v1.65.0/: 01_DELTA.md whose line 1 reads `Delta: LibKa0s v1.69.0 -> v1.70.0 (span: v1.69.0 v1.70.0)` (span names only the unrecorded tags, first included, per the command spec; NOT the audit's v1.68.1-v1.70.0 shape), with per-file minor changes per tag, and 05_SUMMARY.md with one line per tag (carried, nothing adopted; vendoring commits 5075fd5 / 4c16982 cited by sha). (5) The v1.71.0 bundle docs/revendor/<today>-v1.71.0/: 01_DELTA.md line 1 `Delta: LibKa0s v1.70.0 -> v1.71.0`, per-file LibStub minors (Env 2, Slash key 20.2, Widgets/LineChart/Autocomplete minors, OptionsIdList 4, kit 38), both payload diffs summarised, which majors AbsorbTracker consumes, contract changes under unmoved signatures (Env drops the bare-global GetAddOnMetadata rung: core/EnvSetup.lua's own library-absent fallback is unaffected; confirm). 02_CANDIDATES.md lists new surfaces (Kit.secret, ChartMath.ClipSegment, ParseValue nan/inf refusal, ...) each as `not adopted in this run` with one-line reason; 03_DECISIONS.md records the same; 05_SUMMARY.md. Widgets adoption is handled by AT-02, so it is named there as planned, not as a candidate. (6) Nothing outside libs/LibKa0s/, tests/_kit/, CLAUDE.md, docs/test-cases.md, README.md (badge only, if needed) and docs/revendor/ changes. Commit subject `RV-AT: re-vendor LibKa0s v1.71.0; span bundle v1.69.0-v1.70.0`.
items.steps:
1. `git -C ../LibKa0s tag -l v1.71.0` exists (local). Export the tag to a scratch dir; rsync --delete its LibKa0s/ into libs/LibKa0s/ and testkit/ into tests/_kit/.
2. Roll the CLAUDE.md provenance line.
3. Run the gate; tests/test_vendor_sync.lua must pass against the new payload. If any suite reds on a contract change, stop and record it in 01_DELTA.md as an adoption blocker and fix in this commit only if it is the mechanical consequence of the copy.
4. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md; compare Total with the README badge; roll the badge if they differ.
5. Write docs/revendor/<today>-v1.69.0-v1.70.0/{01_DELTA.md,05_SUMMARY.md} from `git -C ../LibKa0s diff v1.68.1 v1.69.0 -- LibKa0s testkit` and `v1.69.0 v1.70.0`.
6. Write docs/revendor/<today>-v1.71.0/{01_DELTA.md,02_CANDIDATES.md,03_DECISIONS.md,05_SUMMARY.md}.
7. Gate, then commit.

items.title: Offline perf measures the shipped doRepaint: NS.Timer.__doRepaint seam, repaintPass scenario, re-derived dormant ceiling
items.spec: Review C-1. modules/Timer.lua: publish the file-local doRepaint as the suite seam `NS.Timer.__doRepaint = doRepaint` beside the existing NS.Timer.__ev seam, with a comment saying it is a test seam only (no production caller). No behaviour change. tests/perf.lua: (a) scenario 3 `paintPass` (:196-197, which wraps NS.ForEachUnit/NS.UpdateAbsorbBar in a test closure) is renamed `paintBars` and keeps its 12-API-calls assertion; (b) a new `repaintPass` scenario calls NS.Timer.__doRepaint() directly per iteration (re-arming nothing; doRepaint clears `pending` itself), asserting apiPerIter == 12 too; (c) scenario 6 probeOverheadOff/probeOverheadOn (:224-229) move onto NS.Timer.__doRepaint() so the dormant/armed comparison runs the outer repaintPass bracket, the `parent` derivation and doRepaint's own fan-out; (d) PROBE_OFF_BYTES_CEILING is re-derived by the method its comment documents (three runs of the dormant arm, measured figure + headroom smaller than one empty table, the one-`{}` cost re-measured under this interpreter) and the RE-BASELINED comment block is rewritten with the date and the three numbers. The current per-pass closure (expected ~144 B/iter vs the 72 B ceiling) is what the new figure includes: set the ceiling from the measurement as it stands on this commit (AT-05 later removes the closure and lowers it). docs/performance.md:72-77 (the offline scenario table / prose naming paintPass and the 48.0 B figure) describes the new scenario set and figures. A perf-runner assertion that fails exits non-zero, so `lua tests/perf.lua` must exit 0.
items.steps:
1. Add the seam in modules/Timer.lua (one line + comment).
2. Red first: point probeOverheadOff at the seam with the OLD 72 ceiling and run `lua tests/perf.lua`; record that it reds (the closure + bracket are now measured) in the commit message as the proof the old gate missed the shipped path.
3. Rename paintPass -> paintBars, add repaintPass, re-derive the ceiling (3 runs, plus the one-`{}` probe) and rewrite the comment.
4. Update docs/performance.md:72-77.
5. Gate + `lua tests/perf.lua` exit 0; commit `AT-01: ...`.

items.title: LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0 gets its setup seam: core/WidgetsSetup.lua publishes NS.Widgets with a library-absent stub and a parity case
items.spec: Option A of AT-A-07 (library-stack: one setup file per adopted module, degrading to a stub; testing-§8 parity per adopted module). New core/WidgetsSetup.lua, shaped like core/PerfSetup.lua / core/LauncherSetup.lua: resolves `LibStub("LibKa0s-Widgets-1.0", true)` once and publishes NS.Widgets = the live major, or, when absent, a stub carrying exactly the members AbsorbTracker reaches: DragHandle (a function answering nil, so NS.CreateBar draws no strip, as today) and DRAG_HANDLE = nil semantics preserved by the consumers (the stub publishes no DRAG_HANDLE table, or one the consumers treat as zero room; pick the shape that keeps HANDLE_ROOM = 0 and say so in the comment). modules/Bar.lua:15 and modules/Display.lua:26-28 stop calling LibStub and read NS.Widgets instead; their nil-guards are reduced to the stub contract (Bar draws a strip only when NS.Widgets.DragHandle returns a frame; Display derives HANDLE_ROOM from NS.Widgets.DRAG_HANDLE or 0). Comments at Bar.lua:10-14 and the docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:49-51 passage that says 'there is no core/<Name>Setup.lua seam' are rewritten. AbsorbTracker.toc: `core\WidgetsSetup.lua` in the # Core block before modules\Bar.lua is reached (place it after core\CoreSetup.lua if the stub uses NS.LIBKA0S_MISSING, otherwise with the other setup seams), annotated `# LOAD-BEARING: publishes NS.Widgets, captured as a file-scope upvalue by modules/Bar.lua and modules/Display.lua.` (toc-file-§5). tests/run.lua registers nothing new unless suites are listed explicitly (check; add the file to any explicit load list, wow_mock/degraded_env TOC readers follow the TOC). tests/test_surface_parity.lua: new case `parity: the Widgets stub carries every Widgets member the addon reaches` enumerating the reached members by name (DragHandle, DRAG_HANDLE) against the live major, in the style of the Perf case (:241). tests/test_draghandle.lua or tests/test_widgets.lua: a degraded-load case asserting no strip is drawn and HANDLE_ROOM is 0 with the library absent (reuse loadDegraded from tests/degraded_env.lua). docs/module-map.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md module map gain the file. No register row (Option B) is needed once the seam exists.
items.steps:
1. Red first: add the parity case and the degraded-load case referencing NS.Widgets; run and see them fail (NS.Widgets nil). '-- red under:' notes on both.
2. Write core/WidgetsSetup.lua and the annotated TOC line; switch Bar.lua and Display.lua to NS.Widgets.
3. tests/test_loadorder.lua (if it pins the TOC listing) and any explicit file lists updated.
4. Docs: ARCHITECTURE.md:49-51, module map, docs/module-map.md.
5. regenerate docs/test-cases.md (`lua tests/run.lua --list > docs/test-cases.md`, CRLF per the repo's .gitattributes) and roll the README Tests badge to the new Total in the same commit (testing-§5).
6. Gate; commit `AT-02: ...`.

items.title: doRepaint iterates NS.Units.LIST directly instead of building a closure per coalesced pass
items.spec: Review C-2. modules/Timer.lua doRepaint (:40-42): replace `NS.ForEachUnit(function(unit) ... end)` with `for _, unit in ipairs(NS.Units.LIST) do if NS.UpdateAbsorbBar(unit, parent) then painted = true end end` (or a numeric for over the list), so a coalesced pass allocates no closure, matching the file header's hoisting rationale (:13-16). Behaviour identical: same unit order (ForEachUnit iterates NS.Units.LIST - confirm in core/Units.lua), same painted/NoteRepaint/Perf.Note accounting. No suite stubs NS.ForEachUnit (verified in the assessment; re-grep). tests/perf.lua: AT-01's repaintPass / probeOverheadOff figures drop by the closure's cost; re-derive PROBE_OFF_BYTES_CEILING again by the documented method and rewrite the RE-BASELINED block (before/after bytes recorded in the comment and the commit message). docs/performance.md figures follow.
items.steps:

2. Red first: lower PROBE_OFF_BYTES_CEILING to the expected closure-free figure + headroom and see `lua tests/perf.lua` fail on the current code.
3. Replace the closure with the loop; perf goes green.
4. Rewrite the baseline comment; docs/performance.md.
5. Gate + perf; commit `AT-05: ...` with before/after figures.

items.title: NS.RelockForCombat: standing up or enabling mid-combat re-locks unlocked bars so the fight starts on live data
items.spec: Review C-5. core/AbsorbTracker.lua: extract the re-lock half of addon:OnEnterCombat (:318-321: `if not NS.GetSetting("locked") then NS.SetByPath("locked", true); NS.Print("Bars locked — combat started"); NS.RefreshOptionsPanel() end`) into `function NS.RelockForCombat()` returning true when it re-locked. OnEnterCombat calls it and keeps its EITHER/OR (publish VISIBILITY+REPAINT only when it did not re-lock). core/Lifecycle.lua StandUp, at its end (after the POSITION/APPEARANCE/REPAINT publishes), and addon:OnEnable's running path (core/AbsorbTracker.lua, after the bars are placed; covers /reload mid-combat on an unlocked profile) call NS.RelockForCombat() when `UnitAffectingCombat("player")` is true. The chat line may read 'Bars locked — in combat' on the stand-up path (the shared helper takes the reason, or prints one neutral line; keep one literal per reason). No new event registration; respects the stood-down latch (StandUp runs after release). Comments in docs/lifecycle.md (the stand-up rebuild) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md -> The disabled state is total gain one sentence on the in-combat stand-up. tests: +2 cases (tests/test_disabled.lua for '/at enable mid-combat on an unlocked profile re-locks and prints once'; tests/test_events.lua or tests/test_visibility.lua for 'OnEnable while in combat on an unlocked profile re-locks'), each with a '-- red under:' note; the existing OnEnterCombat re-lock cases stay green. wow_mock must answer UnitAffectingCombat (check; add a settable flag only if missing).
